cells.tense: You are passing meaning on right now, adjusting it as it goes.
cells.act: add a little or take a little away, and sense the difference
cells.ask: Take a saying or a way of doing something you were handed. Add a piece of your own to it, or drop a piece. Make just that change, then stop and feel how it sits.
cells.core:
You carry what's been handed down and you have a light touch with it. A phrase, a way of doing a thing, a story someone told you — it goes through you to the next person changed just enough to fit, still recognisable as what it was, and nobody feels pushed into it. That is what keeps a shared thing alive rather than stuffed.

At the moment before anything has chosen, that touch is available to you now. So change a small part of what you pass on and stop there — the way you'd season a dish and then leave it alone. You'll have handed on something that's yours and theirs at once, and you'll know which parts of it are load-bearing by noticing what shifts.
cells.sheetLine: You pass it on, and it stays alive.
cells.verb: handing forward what proved worth keeping
cells.place: the quiet before anything has chosen yet

cells.tense: You will hand it on, and it will not be allowed to change.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: Pick a rule or tradition you've been keeping exactly as it was given to you. For one day, don't enforce the usual form. Watch what actually falls, and don't rush to prop it back up.
cells.core:
You hold the form of what's been handed to you so hard it can't move. Every telling of it has to match the last, every person has to do it the same, and anything unfamiliar gets kept outside, including the ones who come carrying it with them. What was meant to pass something living along has turned into a lock on it.

Let one of those forms come down and don't put it back up. Somewhere you've been enforcing a version of something, stop for one day: let the thing be done differently, and don't correct it. When it falls you'll see what was holding nothing up. Then, out of what's left standing, you can take something looser in your hands.
cells.sheetLine: You've sealed it against anything unexpected.

cells.tense: You used to have something to hand on, and it is not with you now.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Think of a few times lately you figured something out on your own. Write one line on how each was built. Read that page back once, decide nothing about it, and do nothing more.
cells.core:
There is no shared thing you can reach for here, so each time you come to something true you come to it alone, and it starts over for the next person. The old stories, the ways of doing it that would carry you, aren't near you. What you know holds, and it has nothing under it.

So pull the shape out of a few of your own discoveries and see the method underneath them, without any of the specifics you found. That's the part that can be handed on; the details were never the point. Keep the page. It can be the start of something you pass along rather than keep re-inventing, and if it isn't, you still know how you work.
cells.sheetLine: You work it all out alone and start over each time.
cells.verb: handing forward what proved worth keeping

cells.tense: You are already passing it on and your hand is not on the pen.
cells.act: find the centre and hold it while things move
cells.ask: Notice a thing you do that someone near you has picked up — a phrase, a habit, a way of deciding. Stay with it as it is for a day, without steering it, and watch what it does.
cells.core:
Those close to you are already carrying things they got from you, and you don't count yourself as the source. Somebody says a thing the way you say it, handles a problem the way you handle it, and you'd tell anyone the influence came from somewhere else. It is happening. It is yours.

So hold still with a habit you pass on and let it move without your hand on it — a phrase, a way you meet a small decision. Not a change, just attention, and then let the day go. You'll feel what it's like to be near something you're already shaping without noticing, and by evening you'll likely spot your own mark somewhere you hadn't looked.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the source of it.
cells.verb: handing forward what proved worth keeping
cells.place: the quiet before anything has chosen yet
